### Non-VERIFIED items

### [1] PARTIAL. CN 987869 page 1 (iluxo shelving reason)
- Claim (citations.md; prior-art.md row 4/"False trips" item): iluxo "shelved because an ASIAIR meridian flip stops 'approx 5 millimeters' from the tripod".
- Source (iluxo, 2025-12-19): "I started to work on a solution but shelved it for the time being... this opened a whole can of worms to train it, so it learns where the no-go-zone is... when its doing a meridian flip it stops with the backend of the scope really close to the tripod (approx 5 millimeters)... This implies that to avoid unecessary "emergency stops" it has to pretty accurate. Family life is busy at the moment so I shelved it".
- Issue: stated shelving reasons are training difficulty and lack of time. The 5 mm figure is cited as an accuracy requirement, not as the reason for shelving. The quotes themselves ("opens a relay and kills the power to the mount", "approx 5 millimeters") are exact. The main deliverable's use ("legitimate flips can pass within about 5 mm of the tripod [1]") is supported.
- All other [1] content verified (Bob4BVM "Real protection is done with proper sensors... a contactor to break the power to motor"; momo-chan "Does it power off the mount, or just stop? Recovery methods would also be necessary."; ButterFly "It's only where the sensor is that you will detect trouble"; astroneer3141 reed/magnet "work only for a particular DEC angle"; dates and authors match).

### [12] PARTIAL. CN 877344 (misattributed quote, wrong mount)
- Claim (citations.md; built-in-protection.md row "Celestron (worm)"): speedster (CGX-L) ... "There is no torque limiter, current detector, or anything of the sort" (Celestron).
- Source: speedster (2023-05-27) wrote "the computer lost control of the mount (CGX-L)... the mount had continued to drive it into the pier for hours." The "no torque limiter" sentence is by a different poster, ButterFly (2023-05-30), about an AVX: "There is no torque limiter, current detector, or anything of the sort. When my 120mm refractor on my AVX strikes the tripod leg, the motors impart enough force that the scope slips in RA in its slip clutch... Slipping in the clutch is not a safety feature".
- Issue: quote is real but belongs to ButterFly and concerns an AVX that has a slip clutch, not the CGX-L. The citations.md entry runs the two together under speedster. The "for hours" claim is verified.

### [18] PARTIAL. CN 987276 (NINA has no travel-limit setting)
- Claim: "NINA has no general travel-limit setting" (citations.md; built-in-protection.md "No general travel limit").
- Source: archiebald (2025-12-11): "when I asked a question in this forum a very rude software developer shouted me down... Therefore, unless something has changed, as far as I know, there is nothing similar in NINA." momo-chan: "I am considering situations where collisions occur within the range of not crossing the meridian."
- Issue: the source is one user's hedged recollection, stated in the docs as fact. No NINA documentation or developer statement in the thread. (The [48] NINA page is outside this audit's scope.)

### [19] PARTIAL. CN 931532 (context shift)
- Claim (power-loss-behavior.md "Observed behavior when unpowered"): "Without clutches, users note that strain wave mounts are 'completely dependent on power' [19]."
- Source (TransitVanMan, 2024-09-04): "Without clutches you're completely dependent on power. When the battery runs out you can't carry on with low and medium powers and 'push' RA." The context is visual use, not holding behavior on power loss. The pier-extension quote ("it doesn't prevent the camera from hitting the tripod legs") is verified but is by Brian Carter (2025-04-13), not TransitVanMan; citations.md does not attribute it, so no error there.
- Issue: the quote is accurate but is about being unable to move the mount by hand when unpowered, placed under unpowered-position-holding evidence.

### [27] PARTIAL. ZWO forum 14643 (overreach in use)
- Quotes verified: Sam@ZWO "Seems the power supply is not enough and causes the mount to reboot"; ASIMount@ZWO "We recommend 12V 3A power for AM5 itself."
- Issue 1: built-in-protection.md ("Recovery" table) says "Reboots on supply loss". Source says an insufficient supply (hedged "Seems") causes a reboot, with reference to red/green flashing and re-sync. It is not about loss of supply.
- Issue 2: main deliverable R15 uses it to "Size the switch for mount supply current". The source is a recommended supply rating, not a measured mount current draw. The R15 text says "e.g.", so it is soft.
- Sam@ZWO's reply was about the light/re-sync problem, not the grinding stop in post 1; citations.md's "Grinding then stop; Sam@ZWO..." joins them.

### Per-citation results

**[43] VERIFIED.** 10Micron brochure: "Absolute encoders directly mounted on both RA & Dec axes"; "High-precision traditional worm-wheel drives". Used for the 10Micron absolute-encoder row.

**[44] VERIFIED.** AP PDF: "If the mount is not parked before power down, it may begin tracking when next powered up." Note: the PDF also says chips earlier than the "S" chip track immediately and that Auto-connect=YES begins tracking on power-up, so "some mounts can" (R13) is well founded.

**[45] VERIFIED.** ASCOM: "It is permissible for the mount to require power cycling before being unparked (with Unpark() ) and used."

**[46] VERIFIED.** EQASCOM PDF: limits apply to Tracking and Gotos; not applied to "Manual slews initiated by the EQASCOM direction pad or external gamepad"; "As these limits use encoder positions they can only be applied properly if the mount is parked and unparked."

**[47] VERIFIED.** indilib/indi #556, opened Apr 6, 2018 by Atlas8m: "When I manually nudge the mount, the mount will not stop slewing even if it passes the meridian, which may damage the mount."

**[48] VERIFIED.** NINA docs: "Meridian flips prevent that your telescope and camera bump into the mount and do major damage to your equipment." Cited only alongside [18] for the "no general travel limit" point, which [48] does not itself make (it is carried by [18]).

**[49] VERIFIED.** Gemini-2: "the Safety limits depend on a good CWD position of the RA axis"; limits stored as "physical step" values; "It a very bad idea to start up with a 'Warm Restart' and assume that the Gemini 2 has remembered the CWD."

**[50] VERIFIED.** TIMSENS, dated Aug 26, 2026: "With an incremental encoder, any power interruption — a trip, a brownout, a deliberate shut-down — erases the position count. Recovery forces a homing routine". Vendor marketing, tier 4 as stated.

**[51] VERIFIED.** IceInSpace post #2, 01-01-2023, mldee: "Received a response from ZWO via the FB AM5 group that the ASCOM driver currently does not have a mount limits function, but stops tracking at the meridian."

**[52] PARTIAL.** Quote exists: "It turns out that the mount software from ZWO turns off tracking when the meridian flip limits are reached." But the poster (Bob2023CL, 2024-07-05) is describing their AM3 ("When I got my AM3 one of the first things I did..."), in a thread titled for the AM5. built-in-protection.md uses [51],[52] for "AM5 stops tracking at meridian limit". [51] supports AM5; [52] supports AM3 and the generic "ZWO mount software". Suggested fix: describe [52] as an AM3 owner report, or drop it from the AM5 row.

**[53] PARTIAL.** Quote exists: "when DST changed the ASIAir didn't know how to correctly calculate LST (it was off by 1 hr)... my rig was 1cm away from crashing into the pier." The same sentence continues "I think they fixed that." The doc (built-in-protection.md table, prior-art.md table) states "fixed by ZWO later" as fact, citing [26],[53]. [53] gives only a hedged recollection, and the poster adds that ZWO "can't seem to get things working smoothly after each update". The near-miss claim is verified. Suggested fix: "(poster believes fixed)".

**[54] VERIFIED.** NTRS abstract (abstract only, as disclosed): "A high ratio harmonic drive is non-backdrivable because its output shaft cannot be turned by applying a torque on it." Note: the same abstract defines backdrivability as the output shaft turning "via finite amount of torque" and treats non-backdrivability as a dynamic-model property (sensitivity transfer function), so the doc's "conflict" with [55]/[56] is partly one of framing. The quote is accurate.

**[55] VERIFIED.** Nabtesco: "Strain wave gears and cycloidal gears are fundamentally reversible—when reversing, only the friction needs to be overcome."; "complete self-locking cannot be guaranteed". Note: the second quote is in the passage about Nabtesco's own gears with adjustable backdriving torque; the first is general.

**[56] VERIFIED.** Frontiers (López García, Crispel, Saerens, Verstraten et al.): "Strain Wave trains show large load-independent losses and no-load starting torques—particularly in back-driving conditions". Table 2 lists forward/reverse no-load starting torque for 1:100 Harmonic Drive (2014) units: 17/20% and 10/13% of nominal input torque. These are finite values, as the doc says.

**[57] VERIFIED.** Source Robotics, November 25, 2024: "many harmonic drives are equipped with brakes or clutches to protect against high-impulse inputs, such as crashes or rapid balance corrections in legged robotics". Also states backdrivability depends on ratio (10,000:1 is "virtually impossible to backdrive").

**[58] VERIFIED.** Rockwell MOTION-AT003C-EN-P, April 2019: "Holding brakes are not designed to stop a rotating motor shaft... If the drive main input power fails... the brakes can withstand infrequent use as a stopping brake. However, use of these holding brakes as stopping brakes creates rotational mechanical backlash that is potentially damaging to the system". Note: the source concerns Kinetix servo-motor holding brakes, not mount or harmonic-drive brakes; the doc applies it as an "industrial note" by analogy.

**[59] VERIFIED.** Physical AI Lab: "Safe Torque Off prevents the drive from producing motor torque but does not mechanically lock the axis."; "Do not rely on gearbox friction as a safety-rated holding function."

**[60] VERIFIED.** Arcbotix: cutting power to a motor on a load-bearing joint "lets the joint free-fall until something else stops it"; spring brake re-engages "in tens of milliseconds" (also "20 to 80 ms"). Context is a gravity-loaded arm joint; the doc cites it in a table of engineering sources without that qualifier.

**[61] VERIFIED.** ICNavigator: "a hard brake engagement injects a torque impulse through the output flange into the harmonic drive."

**[62] VERIFIED.** UR forum, March 2023: "a UR10e with ver 5.13 will drop when powered off"; efn: "The brakes will get worn, if the robot has a fair amount of emergency stops and/or shut downs." Note: a single worn-brake report, and power-loss-behavior.md phrases it as "Robot arm 'will drop when powered off'" without that qualifier.

**[63] VERIFIED.** Arcsec, published 2026-07-16: "Exceed it — a crash, a hard stop from full speed, a seized tool — and the flexspline deforms enough for its teeth to jump the mesh... it's the one failure that happens in a millisecond."; "A drive that has ratcheted is permanently altered"; "use current limits in the drive or mechanical stops". All uses (README, main, power-loss, estop) match.

**[64] VERIFIED.** MDPI Machines 12(11):776 (reader file; Politecnico di Torino affiliation present; published 5 November 2024): "when an excessive load is applied while the input shaft is stationary, the FS tends to experience buckling"; ratcheting scenarios "involving sudden impacts, such as when the robot collides with a human operator or an external object". The estop doc's step that a powered-off mount pressed against an obstacle is in this state is labelled inference, which is appropriate.

**[65] VERIFIED.** Harmonic Drive brochure 1064633 06/2025: the torque signal "enables fundamental safety functions in collaborative robots (cobots), such as collision detection"; sensor accuracy "0.1% of the full scale torque".

**[66] VERIFIED (orphan).** ManualsLib SHA-Y: "The brakes equipped on SHA-Y series actuators are used to hold the motor shaft in place when the power is cut off"; "Dry non-excitation actuation type". Not cited anywhere in the prose.

**[67] VERIFIED.** US12416334B1: inventors Dylan Thrush, Kevin Sweeney; Agility Robotics; filed 2022-08-19; published 2025-09-16; slip clutch lets the intermediate member rotate above a torque limit; "a clutched strain wave drive known in the art" is described.

**[68] VERIFIED.** ISO 13850:2015 preview. §4.1.1.2: "it shall be maintained until it is manually reset"; "it shall not be possible for any start command to be effective on those operations stopped"; "The reset shall not initiate machine start up." §4.1.1.3: "complementary protective measure"; §4.1.1.4 note: "continuing operation of auxiliary equipment such as magnetic chucks or braking devices"; §4.1.1.5: "without creating additional hazards"; §3.1: "initiated by a single human action". All section references are correct.

**[69] VERIFIED (orphan).** ISO page: "Stage: 90.92 (To be revised)"; ISO/AWI 13850 listed. Not cited in the prose.

**[70] VERIFIED.** Pilz FAQ (reader file): "the emergency stop may only be reset directly on the emergency stop device on which the command was initiated and by intentional human action." Also says reset only once the hazard is safely removed, which supports R4's "after the obstacle is cleared".

**[71] VERIFIED.** Machinery Safety 101: "The emergency stop command must be maintained until manually reset... and resetting the emergency stop function must not restart the machine on its own, but only permit its restart."; minimum PL "c" under ISO 13849-1; "single-channel architectures can achieve the required Performance Level with suitable component selection."

**[72] VERIFIED.** Machinery Safety 101 (2021-05-19): disengagement of the E-stop device resets the function; IEC 60204-1 text "The reset of the command shall not restart the machinery but only permit restarting."

**[73] VERIFIED.** Engineering Shield: "The mere fact that the cycle does not restart automatically is not sufficient."; three separate actions (release device, reset safety function, process start-up). Published 6 July 2026.

**[74] VERIFIED.** Schneider FA122781: "Category 0: stopping by immediate cutting off of power to the actuators ( example: uncontrolled stop)."

**[75] VERIFIED.** GT Engineering: "Machines with moving parts without inertia and whose stop does not cause additional risks require stop in Category 0."; "A category 0 emergency stop is equivalent to the STO (Safe Torque Off) function". Note: the source states the Category 0 criterion and, separately, that machines with inertia need Category 1. The doc's "Category 0 is acceptable only if" is the converse of the source's two statements. It is labelled inference, so it is acceptable.

**[76] VERIFIED.** Bernstein: separation "must not depend on components such as springs"; "high inrush currents, inductive loads or long switching cycles can lead to welding or contact erosion."

**[77] VERIFIED.** Honeywell 002427 (footer 04/21): "In the case of a weld of the contacts, the action of the actuator will mechanically break the weld, opening the switch contacts."

**[78] VERIFIED.** ISO 13856-2:2013 preview defines 3.15 pre-travel, 3.17 overtravel, 3.19 reset, 3.21 start interlock. Pre-travel is correctly paraphrased as travel from contact to output OFF.

**[79] VERIFIED (orphan).** ISO page: "last reviewed and confirmed in 2024. Therefore this version remains current"; stage 90.93. Not cited in the prose.

**[80] VERIFIED.** RepRap: "The Normally Closed logic is the one more commonly used and suggested as it provides an additional safety in case of failure." Note: this is a 3D-printer signal-wire convention, and the doc uses it as an NC fail-safe basis (R8/R9) by analogy.

**[81] VERIFIED.** RAD: "This event opens a normally closed switch sending a signal to your system's E-stop or controller."; "Stops the robot* within 2 to 10ms of a collision"; "Automatically resets". The asterisk on "robot*" and "robot arm*" is on the page, and no footnote text exists in the fetched file, so "footnote not captured" is accurate.

**[82] VERIFIED.** ATI: "Standard auto reset helps avoid downtime."; the Protector "sends a signal back to the robot controller before or during a collision". Note: the word "breakaway" in citations.md does not appear in the fetched text; it is descriptive only and no claim depends on it.

**[83] VERIFIED.** SCHUNK OPS: "Integrated monitoring for signal transmission without delay in case of collisions so that the robot can be stopped immediately". The page gives no reset information, matching "Not stated".
